content.theory: Modern web pages are multimedia documents. Images, audio, and video make content engaging — but each media type comes with its own semantics, accessibility rules, and performance traps. Get the attributes right and your page loads fast and works for everyone; get them wrong and you ship broken icons and media that hijack screen readers. ### Images: src, alt, and dimensions The `` element is self-closing and needs two things: **src** (the URL of the image) and **alt** (a text description). The `alt` attribute is not decorative — when an image fails to load, the alt text is what your visitor sees, and when a screen reader encounters the image, it announces the alt text. Decorative images that add nothing should use `alt=""` so assistive tech skips them entirely. ```html ``` Setting **width** and **height** prevents layout shift (CLS) while the image downloads, and `loading="lazy"` defers off-screen images until the user scrolls to them — a big win for bandwidth and page speed. ### figure and figcaption When an image (or media block) needs a caption, wrap it in `
